works.title: ValYOU
works.description: A web application designed to automate an ARTA-compliant Customer Satisfaction Survey system. Managed the full documentation process including process flows, compliance records, and design assets using Google Docs, Excel, and Canva.
works.substoryLore: Faced with complex Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA) compliance requirements for citizen feedback, led the structured documentation architecture—translating regulatory mandates into clear process flows, data schemas, and accessible UI assets.

caseStudy.pitch: AN ARTA-COMPLIANT CUSTOMER SATISFACTION SURVEY WEB APPLICATION BUILT TO AUTOMATE CITIZEN FEEDBACK AND SERVICE QUALITY AUDITING.
caseStudy.credits: Documentation Lead & Visual Asset Direction by Jehrome Martin • Pamantasan Ng Lungsod Ng Valenzuela

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.body: Public service offices operating under Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA) mandates struggle with paper-based citizen satisfaction surveys. Manual tallying delays service quality reports, introduces human transcription errors, and makes real-time compliance auditing difficult to sustain.
highlights: Paper-based citizen feedback forms caused slow manual encoding
Strict ARTA Citizen's Charter & Service Quality Dimension (SQD) compliance requirements
Fragmented record keeping across departments without standardized process flows

solution.heading: The Solution
solution.body: ValYOU digitizes the entire ARTA Customer Satisfaction Measurement (CSM) lifecycle into a responsive web platform. As Documentation Lead, I architected the end-to-end process flows, regulatory data schemas, compliance manuals, and UI design assets—bridging legal ARTA mandates with an intuitive digital experience.

features.title: STANDARDIZED SERVICE QUALITY DIMENSIONS MAPPED DIRECTLY INTO THE WORKFLOW
features.description: Translated official ARTA Citizen's Charter guidelines into structured digital survey questionnaires covering responsiveness, reliability, integrity, and outcome metrics.
highlights: Full alignment with ARTA Memorandum Circular CSM standards
Clear bilingual/accessible prompt structure for citizens
Automated categorization by office, service type, and client classification

features.title: END-TO-END TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION GUIDING EVERY DEVELOPMENT SPRINT
features.description: Authored comprehensive system flowcharts, data dictionaries, and compliance records in Google Docs and Excel so developers and stakeholders worked from a single source of truth.
highlights: Data Flow Diagrams (DFD) & entity relationship mapping
Step-by-step user manuals and administrative audit guides
Structured Excel test matrices verifying form validation rules

features.title: CLEAN, FRICTIONLESS INTERFACE ASSETS DESIGNED FOR FAST PUBLIC SUBMISSION
features.description: Crafted cohesive visual banners, iconography, and form layout references using Canva and Figma to ensure visitors can complete feedback in under two minutes on any device.
highlights: Mobile-first survey layout reducing drop-off rates
Visual rating scales for rapid citizen comprehension
Unified branding across digital forms and printable documentation

works.title: Shadow of the Past
works.description: A slasher horror game built around an atmospheric, real-camera video experience. Developed the complete spatial map layout and game environmental layers to create an immersive, tension-filled cinematic atmosphere.
works.substoryLore: Designed the complete spatial map architecture and environmental layering for Bakunawa Studios' slasher horror title. Balanced sightlines, choke points, and found-footage camera framing to sustain dread from start to finish.
works.weakness: Predictable Jump Scares (Solved via Spatial Tension)

caseStudy.pitch: AN ATMOSPHERIC FOUND-FOOTAGE SLASHER HORROR GAME ENGINEERED AROUND CLAUSTROPHOBIC SPATIAL LEVEL DESIGN AND REAL-CAMERA TENSION.
caseStudy.credits: Lead Game Designer & Spatial Level Architect: Jehrome Martin • Produced with Bakunawa Studios

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.body: Many indie horror games rely on loud, repetitive jump scares that quickly lose their impact once players memorize the timing. Sustaining genuine psychological dread requires level geometry, sightlines, and environmental storytelling that make the player feel hunted even in silence.
highlights: Cheap jump scares cause player desensitization after the first encounter
Open or poorly paced corridors break found-footage camera immersion
Need to guide players organically through dark environments without cluttered HUD markers

solution.heading: The Solution
solution.body: Shadow of the Past frames its slasher narrative through a degraded real-camera VHS lens and deliberate spatial architecture. As Lead Game Designer at Bakunawa Studios, I designed the complete map layout and environmental layers—using tight choke points, occluded sightlines, and diegetic lighting cues to control player pacing and tension.

features.title: CHOREOGRAPHED SIGHTLINES AND CHOKE POINTS THAT SUSTAIN CONSTANT DREAD
features.description: Every corridor, doorway, and blind corner was mapped to limit visibility just enough that players must commit to moving forward before knowing what waits around the bend.
highlights: Asymmetric loop topology preventing safe backtracking
Calculated occlusion zones tailored to the VHS camera's field of view
Paced safe pockets that lower heart rate before major slasher encounters

features.title: DIEGETIC CLUES AND ATMOSPHERIC DETAILS REPLACE ARTIFICIAL UI WAYPOINTS
features.description: Layered props, light pools, and environmental decay directly into the scene hierarchy so players piece together the backstory and navigate naturally through visual contrast.
highlights: Zero-HUD navigation driven by light placement and ajar doors
Environmental narrative artifacts revealing the killer's history
Layered audio-visual triggers tied to spatial zones

features.title: A REAL-CAMERA VIDEO EXPERIENCE THAT AMPLIFIES VULNERABILITY
features.description: Balanced movement speed, camera shake, and flashlight falloff so exploring every room feels like stepping through a recovered slasher tape.
highlights: Analog VHS distortion and scanline depth cues
Narrow flashlight cone forcing deliberate camera sweeping
High-contrast shadow pockets concealing environmental threats

works.title: Piso Politiko
works.description: A hybrid tabletop game that explores Philippine politics through strategic gameplay, social deduction, and resource control.
works.substoryLore: Created a satirical yet deeply strategic hybrid tabletop experience mirroring local political dynamics. Iterated extensively on economy balancing, player negotiation loops, and rulebook clarity for GameCon showcase.
works.weakness: Runaway Leader Problem (Solved via Dynamic Catch-up Mechanics)

caseStudy.pitch: A SATIRICAL HYBRID TABLETOP STRATEGY GAME EXPLORING PHILIPPINE POLITICAL DYNAMICS THROUGH RESOURCE CONTROL AND SOCIAL DEDUCTION.
caseStudy.credits: Lead Game Designer & Systems Balancer: Jehrome Martin • Showcased at GameCon with Bakunawa Studios

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.body: Designing a political strategy tabletop game carries two major traps: heavy civic themes can easily feel like a dry lecture, and competitive resource games frequently suffer from the 'runaway leader' problem where one early advantage decides the match long before the final round.
highlights: Early resource snowballs in tabletop strategy often eliminate player tension by mid-game
Complex political mechanics risk overwhelming new players at live convention booths
Need to balance satirical social commentary with genuinely competitive replayability

solution.heading: The Solution
solution.body: Piso Politiko turns campaign strategy, alliances, and public scrutiny into a fast-moving hybrid tabletop experience. As Lead Game Designer, I engineered the core economy, social deduction triggers, and dynamic catch-up mechanics—refining the rulebook through live GameCon playtesting so every turn sparks table negotiation.

features.title: ANTI-SNOWBALL MECHANICS KEEP EVERY CANDIDATE CONTESTABLE UNTIL THE FINAL VOTE
features.description: Mathematical spreadsheet modeling and iterative playtesting tuned campaign funds, influence tokens, and public exposure penalties so leading players attract higher scrutiny.
highlights: Balanced resource curves preventing uncounterable early leads
Risk-reward campaign actions tying high influence gains to public audit cards
Tuned 30-to-45 minute match length ideal for convention and classroom play

features.title: TABLE TALK, FRAGILE ALLIANCES, AND BLUFFING DRIVE THE CORE PLAYER FANTASY
features.description: Designed action cards and voting phases that reward temporary coalitions while tempting players to defect at pivotal moments.
highlights: Hidden agenda and event modifiers that shift table allegiances
Interactive negotiation phases where every player stays engaged off-turn
Satirical flavor text grounded in recognizable local campaign tropes

features.title: STREAMLINED ONBOARDING TESTED LIVE WITH CONVENTION PLAYTESTERS
features.description: Authored a modular rulebook and quick-reference player aids so new groups at GameCon could learn the rules in under five minutes and jump straight into strategic play.
highlights: 1-page quick-start turn summary for rapid booth onboarding
Iterative rule revisions based on live player observation at GameCon
Expanded into the digital spin-off video game Buwaya Catch

works.title: Buwaya Catch
works.description: A fast-paced video game spin-off of Piso Politiko featuring the iconic crocodile character in an arcade progression loop.
works.substoryLore: Expanded the Piso Politiko universe into digital arcade territory using Unity. Tuned spawn curves, arcade scoring feedback, and hazard escalation to make every 60-second session immediately replayable.
works.weakness: Short Session Fatigue (Solved via Escalating Arcade Combos)

caseStudy.pitch: A FAST-PACED UNITY ARCADE SPIN-OFF OF PISO POLITIKO BUILT FOR INSTANT PICK-UP-AND-PLAY VELOCITY AND HIGH-SCORE MASTERY.
caseStudy.credits: Game Designer & Progression Tuner: Jehrome Martin • Developed in Unity with Bakunawa Studios

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.body: Translating a 40-minute tabletop strategy IP into a digital arcade spin-off requires distilling its satirical identity into seconds. Simple catch-and-dodge arcade games quickly suffer from session fatigue if spawn rates feel flat or if scoring lacks risk-reward depth.
highlights: Flat difficulty curves make endless arcade loops feel repetitive within 60 seconds
Need to capture Piso Politiko's satirical tone in pure kinetic gameplay
Arcade controls must feel snappy and readable at high spawn velocities

solution.heading: The Solution
solution.body: Buwaya Catch stars Piso Politiko's iconic crocodile mascot in a high-tempo Unity arcade loop. I designed the escalating hazard waves, combo multiplier thresholds, and tactile audio-visual feedback—turning a simple movement mechanic into a tight 'one-more-run' high-score chase.

features.title: DYNAMIC WAVE PACING RAMPS UP TENSION WITHOUT UNFAIR DIFFICULTY SPIKES
features.description: Tuned object drop speeds, spawn intervals, and hazard ratios across progressive score tiers so players experience a smooth flow state from warm-up to frantic endgame.
highlights: Phased spawn tables introducing hazards at readable intervals
Guaranteed recovery windows preventing impossible unavoidable patterns
escalating speed tiers that reward predictive positioning

features.title: STREAK SCORING REWARDS AGGRESSIVE MOVEMENT AND CLEAN DODGES
features.description: Added consecutive-catch combo chains and high-value bonus drops that tempt players into dangerous screen edges for leaderboard-breaking runs.
highlights: Combo multiplier decay that encourages active chasing over passive camping
Instant visual and audio hit-markers on streak milestones
distinct silhouettes between high-value pickups and penalty hazards

features.title: BRIDGING TABLETOP SATIRE WITH DIGITAL ARCADE ACCESSIBILITY
features.description: Extended the Piso Politiko universe onto Itch.io, giving convention visitors and online players an instant digital entry point into Bakunawa Studios' flagship IP.
highlights: cohesive character art and thematic continuity with Piso Politiko
60-second session loop tailored for browser and desktop play
Published and playable on Bakunawa Studios' Itch.io page

works.title: Ready-Set-Bag!
works.description: An educational mobile game teaching disaster preparedness and emergency go-bag readiness to Grade 6 students.
works.substoryLore: Spearheading both project management and game design for our BSIT Capstone project. Translating disaster risk reduction curricula for Grade 6 learners into engaging mobile gameplay mechanics with measurable educational retention.
works.weakness: Dry Educational Content (Solved via Gamified Time-Trial Packing)

caseStudy.pitch: AN EDUCATIONAL MOBILE GAME TEACHING DISASTER PREPAREDNESS AND GO-BAG READINESS TO GRADE 6 STUDENTS.
caseStudy.credits: Project Manager & Lead Game Designer: Jehrome Martin • BSIT Capstone at Pamantasan Ng Lungsod Ng Valenzuela

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.body: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) lessons for elementary learners often rely on passive lectures and static checklists. Without hands-on simulation, Grade 6 students struggle to internalize which survival items belong in an emergency Go-Bag and how to react calmly under time pressure.
highlights: Static emergency checklists fail to build procedural memory in young learners
Students frequently confuse non-essential household items with PHIVOLCS-recommended survival gear
Teachers lack an interactive tool to track individual student preparedness comprehension

solution.heading: The Solution
solution.body: Ready-Set-Bag! transforms disaster preparedness into a structured Three-Stage Skill Acquisition mobile game (Cognitive, Associative, and Autonomous phases). Leading both Project Management and Game Design, I architected the Exploration, Packing, and Scenario Quiz gameplay loop alongside a Teacher-Facilitated Dashboard.

features.title: PLAYERS NAVIGATE A SIMULATED HOME TO LOCATE PHIVOLCS-ALIGNED SURVIVAL GEAR
features.description: Students explore familiar rooms—kitchen, bathroom, and bedroom—identifying essential survival supplies from the ground up before emergency timers expire.
highlights: Room-by-room spatial exploration grounded in Filipino household layouts
Three-Stage Skill Acquisition progression (Beginner guided cues → Autonomous time-pressure)
Authentic survival items aligned with PHIVOLCS and OCD preparedness standards

features.title: STRATEGIC INVENTORY PRIORITIZATION WITH REAL-TIME RATIONALE FEEDBACK
features.description: Every collected item carries weight and utility values. If a student exceeds the weight limit, movement slows and they must remove distractors—learning why each item is essential or non-essential through instant contextual feedback popups.
highlights: Drag-and-drop Go-Bag inventory with dynamic weight-limit meter
Contextual feedback popups explaining survival rationale (e.g. why fragile glass or heavy toys are hazards)
Adaptive timers and dramatic panic cues that simulate real evacuation urgency

features.title: POST-RUN SCENARIO QUIZZES SYNC DIRECTLY WITH TEACHER CLASSROOM RECORDS
features.description: After packing, students answer situational earthquake and disaster response questions. Scores and packing accuracy feed directly into the Teacher Dashboard for classroom assessment.
highlights: Situational drag-and-drop and multiple-choice DRRM scenario quizzes
Teacher-Facilitated Mode with class-code sessions and student progress tracking
Complete Game Design Document (GDD) & school playtesting validation
